title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Box
providers.scope_notes: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

controls.name: Enable/disable user authentication app
controls.what: Admins enable or disable a custom OAuth 2.0 app for the enterprise by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > User Authentication Apps
controls.quote: enable custom user authentication applications, such as OAuth 2.0 apps, and

controls_unknown: No admin setting found that blocks developers from generating developer tokens; tokens expire after 60 minutes and inherit the app's scopes and the user's access.
Whether Box offers API source-IP enforcement for app tokens (no admin doc found; Shield/firewall not counted).
Whether new Limited Access (App Token) apps can still be created.
Whether Box SSO requirements constrain OAuth token issuance for managed users (not checked).
Whether app access level (App only vs App + Enterprise) and scopes can be overridden by the admin at authorization time; docs show them set by the developer in the Developer Console.

authentication.summary: Ordinary Box access token generated in the Developer Console for testing. It acts as the user who was signed in to the console when it was generated.

federation.details: Generated manually in the console; no external identity exchange applies.

ip_restriction.boundary: A Box staff community answer describes an enterprise IP allowlist that narrows both web app and API access. Current official documentation of its coverage for developer-token calls was not found; confirm with Box.

renewal.summary: Cannot be refreshed programmatically; generate a new token in the Developer Console.

administration.summary: Any developer with access to the app's Configuration tab can generate one; it carries that user's access within the app's scopes. Revoking it in the console also deletes all webhooks the app created.
administration.conditions: Box says developer tokens are for development and testing only and should not be used in production.

expiry.ui: Fixed 60 min, not configurable or refreshable (Developer Console > Configuration > Generate Developer Token)

reads.ui: Admin Console > Reports > Create Report > User Activity; filter Action types to Downloaded

token_format.notes: Ordinary opaque access token; expires after 60 minutes; cannot be refreshed. Acts as the console user.

log_sources.name: Box Enterprise Events (GET /events, stream_type=admin_logs / admin_logs_streaming)
log_sources.notes: Admin/co-admin with reporting permission. admin_logs: 1 year history; admin_logs_streaming: ~2 weeks live. Admin Console reports: 7 years.

log_sources.name: Box Shield alerts (SHIELD_ALERT in enterprise events)
log_sources.notes: Shield add-on only. Suspicious location/session, anomalous download alerts with ip_info and service_name.

credential_id_fields.notes: User mini object (id, name, login) acting; id 2 = Unknown User

lifecycle_events.notes: Programmatic access by a Box application
Access token revoked; coverage for developer tokens not documented

anomaly_cues: Developer's account making API calls from an IP not matching their recent LOGIN events
Bursts of API-style activity under a human admin/developer account
Repeated short-lived activity windows (~60 min) suggesting regenerated developer tokens
Developer tokens generated on an app in production use (webhooks lost on revoke)

containment.steps: Revoke the token in Developer Console or via POST /oauth2/revoke; it also expires on its own after 60 minutes. Disable the developer's account or the app if generation is the problem.
containment.notes: Revoking a developer token deletes all webhooks created by that app.

sample_query.purpose: Review programmatic access by the developer user; filter created_by.login and compare ip_address to their LOGIN events

unknown: Field distinguishing developer-token use from the user's normal sessions

calls.log_notes: Read event emission not documented; token expires after 60 minutes
